sources: SATURDAY Oct 17 2026 RUN (markets closed; all market fields are Friday Oct 16 US closes or last available tick). HEADLINE: THE SOFT-LANDING READ BROKE. HOT CPI PLUS A 110 DOLLAR OIL SHOCK PLUS AN AI ROUT SENT VIX UP 30 PCT AND FLATTENED THE CURVE TO 33BP - THIS IS A STAGFLATIONARY RISK-OFF CONFIGURATION, NOT THE DE-ESCALATION THE LAST RUN DESCRIBED. INFLATION - THE TRIGGER: September CPI 3.7 pct y/y (released Oct 14), accelerating from 3.4 pct in August and ABOVE the 3.6 pct consensus; core 2.6 pct from 2.4 pct, also above the 2.5 pct forecast (CBS News, Morningstar). Energy plus 20.4 pct y/y, gasoline plus 34.2 pct y/y and plus 9.1 pct m/m - gasoline alone was more than half the monthly increase. September PPI plus 6.3 pct y/y, the biggest gain since 2022 (CNBC Oct 15). The Fed had already hiked in September to 3.75-4.00 pct, its first since 2023; Capital Economics puts odds of another hike at the Oct 27-28 meeting near 50 pct, up from 20 pct before the CPI print. EQUITY VOL - THE BREAK: VIX 21.41 on Oct 16, up 4.97 points on the session and the highest in more than four months (Bloomingbit, Seeking Alpha, CNBC). Prior closes: 16.46 (Oct 15), 16.87 (Oct 14), 15.27 (Oct 13), 15.21 (Oct 12), 14.84 (Oct 9). That is plus 6.57 points - roughly plus 44 pct - versus one week ago. DISCREPANCY NOTED: the repo's own GitHub Action auto-update captured VIX 19.99 at 20:48 UTC on Oct 16; this run uses 21.41, the figure carried by multiple wire sources with an explicit plus 4.97 session delta off the 16.46 Oct 15 close. FRED VIXCLS has not yet posted an Oct 16 official close - it will settle which is right. Either way the direction and magnitude are unambiguous. Seeking Alpha attributes part of the move to hedge fund blowout rumors. Trend up. EQUITIES - WORST WEEK SINCE JUNE: Oct 16 closes S&P 500 7,659.44 (minus 1.09 pct), Nasdaq 26,140.03 (minus 2.14 pct), Dow 52,002.41 (minus 0.34 pct) (TheStreet market wrap). Chip stocks fell an eighth straight day; the selloff broadened from semis into software, with CoreWeave among the losers and AI-debt financing the stated worry (CNN, Bloomberg). The Dow holding while the Nasdaq lost 2 pct is still rotation at the index level, but the eight-day semi streak and the vol spike say it is no longer only rotation. OIL - 110 DOLLAR SHOCK: Brent 109.86 USD/Bbl (TradingEconomics, Oct 16, plus 3.94 USD or plus 3.72 pct on the day), after touching 110 intraday (Bloomberg, Whatfinger). Intraday path was wide - 105.90 at 7:27 AM EDT, testing 110 by 2:34 PM EDT (TheStreet). WTI roughly 97.5 early, about 101 late. Versus 103.13 one week ago that is plus 6.5 pct. The Oct 9 run described oil as a geopolitical premium swinging both ways; this week it only went one way, and it is now feeding directly into the CPI print above. Trend up. RATES - THE CURVE FLATTENED HARD: 2s10s 0.33 (FRED T10Y2Y, Oct 15), from 0.37 (Oct 14), 0.42 (Oct 13), 0.44 (Oct 9), 0.47 (Oct 8). That is 11bp of FLATTENING in a week and the flattest reading of this episode. The mechanism is the hawkish repricing: hot CPI and PPI pull the front end up while the long end rallies on growth and risk-off, which is the classic late-cycle compression. Note the repo's auto-update still carries 0.47, nine sessions stale. Trend down. BREAKEVENS - DOWN DESPITE THE CPI BEAT: 5y5y forward 2.31 pct (FRED T5YIFR, Oct 15), from 2.34 (Oct 14), 2.33 (Oct 13), 2.32 (Oct 9). A new low for the stretch. This is the single most interesting divergence on the board: realised inflation accelerated to 3.7 pct and the oil shock is live, yet long-run market-implied inflation fell. The market is reading the Fed as credible - i.e. pricing hikes that work - rather than pricing an inflation regime change. If this starts rising, the picture gets materially worse. Trend down. BOND VOL - ELEVATED AND RISING: MOVE 102.49 (Investing.com, Oct 15 close), from 99.06 (Oct 14), 101.09 (Oct 13), 98.47 (Oct 9), 100.70 (Oct 8). Up about 4 points on the week. No Oct 16 tick was available; given the session's CPI-driven repricing the true figure is more likely higher. TradingView's TVC-MOVE page served internally contradictory figures this run (100.37 with both minus 4.73 pct and plus 3.45 pct one-day changes) and was not used. Trend up. CREDIT - WIDENED OUT OF THE BAND: HY OAS 325bp (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, 3.25 pct dated Oct 14), from 316 (Oct 13), 311 (Oct 12), 311 (Oct 9), 315 (Oct 8). The 303-312 band flagged last run has BROKEN TO THE WIDE SIDE, and 325 is the widest of this episode - roughly 57bp above the Sep 18 base of 268bp. With the Oct 16 equity rout and vol spike post-dating this print, the next reading is likely wider still. Note the repo's auto-update carries 310, which is stale and understates the move. Trend up. LABOUR - STILL THE STRONG TILE: initial claims 199k for the week ending Oct 10 (DOL advance release Oct 15; FRED ICSA), from 197k (Oct 3), 199k (Sep 26), 198k (Sep 19), 198k (Sep 12). Four straight weeks below 200k. Marginally higher on the week so trend up, but this is noise inside a historically tight range - firms are still not firing, and claims remain the main evidence against a recession read. CONSUMER - FIVE-MONTH LOW, EXPECTATIONS RISING: UMich preliminary October 46.3, from 48.1 final September (Bloomberg, Advisor Perspectives, Verified Investing). One-year inflation expectations 4.7 pct (from 4.6) and five-year 3.5 pct (from 3.4) - both UP, which is the uncomfortable combination with a 34 pct gasoline move. The repo's auto-update still carries 48.1. Trend down. DOLLAR - FELL, WHICH IS THE ODD ONE OUT: DXY 101.782 (TradingEconomics, Oct 16, minus 0.7715 or minus 0.75 pct), from 102.01 one week ago. A dollar that falls on a hawkish CPI surprise is not the textbook reaction; it fits better with the AI-rout-plus-oil-shock story pressuring US assets broadly than with a rates story. Trend down. GROWTH PROXY - UNCHANGED, STILL LOW-QUALITY: 1.57 (copper 6.532 USD/Lbs plus 0.31 pct, gold 4,166.39 USD/t.oz minus 0.11 pct, both TradingEconomics Oct 16; 6.532/4166.39*1000 = 1.568). Identical to last run at the second decimal. Gold came off its highs slightly while copper firmed, so the composition improved even though the ratio did not move. Trend flat. FINANCIAL CONDITIONS - TIGHTENING AT THE MARGIN: NFCI minus 0.499 for the week ending Oct 9 (FRED NFCI), from minus 0.507 (Oct 2), minus 0.517 (Sep 25), minus 0.527 (Sep 18), minus 0.536 (Sep 11). Five consecutive weeks of the index rising, i.e. conditions tightening steadily from a very loose base. Still deeply negative in absolute terms, so this is drift not stress - but it is a consistent one-way drift and it pre-dates the Oct 16 selloff. Next print Oct 21. Trend up (tightening). REAL ECONOMY - ALL CARRIED, NO NEW PRINTS: ISM Manufacturing 54.5 (September, next release Nov 2). Sahm Rule 0.00 (September, FRED SAHMREALTIME, next Nov 6; trigger is plus 0.50 so this is direction not signal). Building permits 1,403k (August; 1,433k July, 1,374k June) - the September release lands Oct 20, three days out. LEI y/y minus 0.7 pct carried; the Conference Board publishes September LEI on Oct 22. All flat. MONETARY PLUMBING - STILL BLIND: Fed funds target 3.75-4.00 pct after the September hike. The 3M SOFR-OIS spread remains unavailable from any free source, so 0bp is CARRIED AS A STANDING ASSUMPTION, as is the EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis at minus 10bp. FRED's /data/SOFR table endpoint served stale 2025 rows this run and was discarded. Global liquidity 1 (stable) - the Fed is hiking rates but no balance-sheet regime change was found; this tile is a judgement call, not a measurement. BDTI DATA FLAG - NINETEENTH consecutive run carried at 4,899 and formally non-informative. No free source served a current value again: Investing.com's scoreboard, Barchart and the Baltic Exchange are subscription-gated and MacroMicro failed. Because the real index tops out near 1,900, the stored 4,899 is NOT on a comparable scale and must not be read as a level. Wire a paid source or drop the tile. INFRASTRUCTURE - THE COMMIT BUG IS FIXED, AND A DUPLICATE WRITER WAS FOUND: (1) The Oct 8 and Oct 9 sessions both wrote data.json and staged it but NEVER COMMITTED, because the sandbox blocked git from unlinking its own lock and temporary objects. This run obtained folder delete permission, cleared a stale .git/HEAD.lock dated Oct 7, and git operations now work normally. (2) MORE IMPORTANT: a GitHub Action is independently auto-updating data.json every day and HAS been succeeding - origin/main was NINE commits ahead of this clone with auto-updates through 'chore: auto-update macro data 2026-10-16'. Local and remote are therefore two writers on the same file. This run reset the local clone to origin/main (discarding a superseded Oct 7 local commit, backed up first) and committed on top. The two writers should be reconciled - either this scheduled session or the Action should own data.json, not both. (3) The Action's output is good on live market prices (its Brent 109.71 and DXY 101.8 match this run within noise) but STALE on the slower series: it carried curve 0.47, HY 310, sentiment 48.1 and claims 197, all of which this run corrects. That is the concrete argument for keeping the session as the writer. (4) SECURITY, UNRESOLVED AND REPEATED: the origin remote is NOT the SSH URL the task prompt describes - it is an HTTPS URL with a GitHub personal access token embedded in plain text in .git/config. That token should be revoked and replaced with the SSH remote. (5) git fetch emitted 'error: Could not read 644e7b1f2e6db6b4c44d26d820a571dddd512a64', suggesting minor object-store damage from the earlier failed runs; operations succeed but a fresh clone would be cleaner. (6) Leftover junk still in the repo root from previous workarounds: _stale_git_locks/ and _wtest, both untracked and safe to delete. PICTURE: last run's reading was that the long-end panic was deflating without the growth picture deteriorating - a soft-landing shape. One week later that has inverted on every axis that matters. Inflation re-accelerated and beat consensus, oil added a 6.5 pct supply-side shock straight into the next print, the Fed is now roughly a coin flip to hike again in eleven days, credit broke out of its band to the wide side, the curve flattened 11bp, equity vol went up 44 pct in a week and the consumer's inflation expectations rose while sentiment hit a five-month low. The two tiles still arguing the other way are claims, which remain below 200k for a fourth week and say nobody is firing, and 5y5y breakevens, which FELL to 2.31 and say the market still believes the Fed will win. That combination - strong labour, anchored long-run expectations, but a live energy shock and a hawkish Fed - is a policy-error setup rather than a recession setup: the risk is not that the economy is rolling over, it is that the Fed tightens into an oil shock. WATCH: the Oct 27-28 FOMC, now roughly 50/50 for a hike; whether 5y5y breakevens hold 2.31 or start pricing a regime change (the single most important tile on this board right now); whether HY OAS keeps widening past 325 after the Oct 16 rout, which this print pre-dates; whether VIX holds above 20 or the spike mean-reverts, and whether the official FRED Oct 16 close comes in nearer 21.41 or the Action's 19.99; whether 2s10s holds 33bp or inverts; whether claims finally break 200k; whether Brent holds above 105; September building permits on Oct 20 and September LEI on Oct 22; NFCI on Oct 21 for the first read that includes the selloff; reconciling the two writers on data.json; and revoking the embedded PAT. Still three assumed or blind tiles out of nineteen (SOFR-OIS, cross-currency basis, BDTI).
